acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Public status/report/lineage/artifacts reflect actual runtime work with stable run/submission/attempt/node/partition links; no acceptance stub masquerades as completion
acceptance.observed_result: The standard SQLModel backend stores actual runtime reports in a tenant/workspace-scoped table. Managed status reads durable worker state, and report/lineage queries return the real report after backend restart. The worker also publishes scoped start/completion events with stable run, submission, plan and attempt identities; the managed transfer recovery test observed events for both attempts after a crash following report persistence. Explicitly durable JSON outputs are persisted under hashed per-run roots; headless and HTTP downloads require the separate run.artifact.content action at run and artifact scope, use bounded SafeIoPolicy reads, and survived service restart in the application and standard SQLModel tests. Lineage queries now include stable run-to-attempt and attempt-to-executed-node edges. The report preserves both the executing attempt and the result-reconciliation attempt when a worker restarts after report publication; the focused managed application/backend and authorization suites passed 89 tests. Runtime report lineage now also links source nodes to bounded, run-scoped opaque partition IDs observed during partition-completeness checks; metadata records source key names and counts without values. Sink/output partition result records and result-retention implementation/qualification remain open.
acceptance.open_reason: Observed source partitions now have bounded run-scoped lineage links, but sink/output partition result records and the complete result-retention campaign remain open; the new lineage path has not received a focused regression run.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Commit-success/report-failure recovers publication without rerunning ETL; result and cleanup state truthfully represent remaining obligations
acceptance.observed_result: Worker report recovery still proves that a committed report is reused after lease expiry and restart without rerunning ETL, including status preservation after a report-write interruption. Artifact cleanup now has focused bounded-batch, filesystem-failure/retry, missing-file, symlink, run-status-preservation, and managed SQLite scope/restart coverage. The managed retention case preserves another scope and reports completed cleanup after restart.
acceptance.open_reason: Persistent report-store outage reconciliation and the complete result publication/cleanup failure, retry and restart matrix remain open; PostgreSQL artifact-retention qualification is not available in this run.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Event resume, duplicates, cursor gaps, pagination, retention and artifact authorization pass reconnect and isolation cases
acceptance.observed_result: The latest focused regression batch passed bounded explicit tombstone pruning and expiry for memory and SQLite stores, including scope isolation, invalid/oversized batch rejection and republishing after expiry. Existing event pagination, reconnect, cursor-gap, authorization and SSE redaction cases also passed in the focused/default suites. Artifact cleanup passed bounded, retry, missing-file and managed SQLite scope/restart cases; durable-content authorization and restart tests remain covered.
acceptance.open_reason: PostgreSQL explicit tombstone-prune/expiry qualification and the complete reconnect plus cross-owner isolation campaign remain open; the latest PostgreSQL-only tests were skipped because no database test URL is configured.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Test/catalog/schema/preflight actions run outside the gateway with action authorization, pagination, deadlines, redaction and scoped receipts
acceptance.observed_result: Durable connector action jobs now have typed secret-free requests, owner-scoped idempotent receipts, bounded pagination, separate fenced worker execution, authorization rechecks, deadlines, cancellation, provider-error redaction and bounded results. The built-in catalog handler and registered test, schema and preflight async handlers passed focused local tests; live PostgreSQL 16.13 multiprocess acceptance and competing worker claims each resolved to one durable action. Provider-specific live action integrations remain unqualified.
acceptance.open_reason: Receipt environment/security-domain isolation and scope-bound cursors were strengthened in the candidate but have not been separately qualified. Provider-specific live connection-test, schema-inspection and preflight integrations, plus the full provider cancellation and credential-isolation matrix, remain open.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Preview executes only in a qualified bounded action role, isolates credentials, limits/redacts returned data and enforces separate retention
acceptance.observed_result: Partial local implementation: preview is admitted as a closed, secret-free request containing only opaque provider, connection and resource references plus limits and redaction fields. The separate action host requires declared columns, applies row and byte caps, redacts provider-sensitive and caller-selected fields, and assigns a separate result expiry. SQLModel cleanup removes expired preview payloads while preserving the receipt across restart. Managed-config, action-host, and durable-store boundaries now enforce a 60–86,400 second TTL, and failed or timed-out jobs cannot retain preview results; this boundary change has not received focused regression qualification.
acceptance.open_reason: No provider-specific preview handler or deployment credential-resolution boundary is shipped and qualified; local tests use a fake provider handler and saved opaque identifiers. The 60–86,400 second TTL is enforced at managed-config, action-host, and durable-store boundaries, and only successful preview jobs can retain results; these boundary changes have not received focused regression qualification.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Explicit provisioning has permission, idempotency, effect and cleanup evidence; ordinary inspection does not create or mutate targets
acceptance.observed_result: Partial local implementation: provisioning has a separate action permission, durable idempotency and a stable action id; the worker forces create-only/if-exists-fail, fingerprints the typed schema, and validates an effect receipt. Cleanup is separately authorized and accepted only for a successful same-owner parent with matching provider, connection, resource, schema and effect. A mock effect store verified create and cleanup; inspection completed without mutating it. Provision schema parsing also rejects nullable primary-key columns; this latest validation has not received focused regression qualification.
acceptance.open_reason: No provider-specific create/cleanup handler is shipped or a real provider effect and compensation qualified; provider operations remain deployment-supplied handlers. The nullable-primary-key validation has not received a focused regression run.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Trusted owner/workload/scope/purpose reaches each worker/action secret and resource access; tampered references and cross-owner cache reuse are rejected
acceptance.observed_result: Partial local evidence: server-derived worker scope reaches secret and storage/connector calls; secret cache is isolated by trusted scope. Managed current-version references require a worker-injected policy, which receives that authenticated scope and blocks provider access when missing or denied. The managed input-resource implementation now records the durable lease ID in accepted and lifecycle-command envelopes; standard workers require exact lease-authorized reads, and the memory and SQLModel stores enforce the finalized owner-bound reference, tenant/workspace scope, live lease, and content digest. This change has not received a focused runtime or cross-process qualification run. Input-resource lease identities now also bind the principal issuer, kind, subject, and environment so separate caller scopes under one resource owner cannot share a deterministic lease ID; lifecycle-command recovery continues to honor stored legacy lease identities, and this change has not received focused runtime or cross-process qualification.
acceptance.open_reason: Action executors, broader tampered-reference policy and full scope-isolation qualification remain incomplete; the environment/principal lease identity and legacy recovery path still require focused runtime and cross-process qualification.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Exact-version and authorized late-binding modes cover rotation/revocation/expiry/outage; actual version is auditable without leaking values
acceptance.observed_result: Partial local evidence: unversioned built-ins reject exact selectors; managed current aliases require runtime authorization before provider or cache access; versioned aliases must be declared and report the resolved version. Managed aliases and providers with lease/renewal/revocation capabilities bypass process caching, and consecutive alias resolutions observe rotation without exposing values. Managed resolution now rejects provider results for a different provider/name/key. Reference invalidation clears matching entries across trusted-scope cache partitions, and a zero-second TTL expires immediately. The identity and cache changes have not received focused regression runs. Secret-cache construction and insertion now reject invalid capacity and non-finite or negative TTL values; a zero TTL removes any matching old value and skips insertion. This cache-boundary change has not received focused regression qualification.
acceptance.open_reason: Provider lease acquisition/renewal/revocation, expiry and outage behavior remain unimplemented end to end or unqualified; the reference-identity and scoped cache invalidation/TTL changes also need focused regression coverage. The latest secret-cache TTL/capacity validation remains unqualified.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Finalized uploads bind immutable version/checksum/length/owner; workers reject tampering, unsafe paths and unsupported format/resource locators
acceptance.observed_result: Migration 010 and the current SQLite-backed managed candidate bind upload version, checksum, byte length, tenant/workspace and owner. Focused evidence covers finalized-reference round trips, cross-owner denial, same-length blob tamper detection, unsupported formats, extra path locators and physical binding-path rejection. The real managed worker parsed UTF-8 BOM/semicolon content after staging TTL and rejected same-length stored-byte tampering after acceptance before writing the sink. The combined input-resource, CSV, HTTP, worker and migration suite passed 56 tests with no skips; the PostgreSQL 16.13 multi-process acquisition/cleanup race passed six forced and simultaneous trials. A fresh Python 3.14.3 wheel install passed migration 010, restart-safe leased reads, scope, blob-integrity and OpenAPI checks.
acceptance.open_reason: The broader worker threat matrix and complete provider security qualification remain open.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Leases protect accepted/retry/replay inputs from retention; aborted uploads, orphans and expired inputs have bounded cleanup and stable outcomes
acceptance.observed_result: Memory and SQLModel upload stores protect accepted references with durable owner-scoped leases, allow reads past staging expiry while a lease is live, and perform bounded expiry/orphan cleanup. Abort is limited to staged uploads. The managed worker rejected the initial run before runtime startup, then executed retry, rerun and replay from the same finalized resource; four durable leases preserved reads beyond staging TTL. HTTP cleanup qualification verifies permission denial, caller-owner scoping, bounded batches, stable candidate counts and idempotent empty cleanup. The combined input-resource, CSV, HTTP, worker and migration suite passed 56 tests with no skips. PostgreSQL 16.13 multi-process lease-versus-cleanup qualification passed six trials, including both serialized orderings and four simultaneous races; no successful lease referred to deleted bytes. The clean Python 3.14.3 wheel smoke verified lease reads after backend restart.
